rules.statement: Build a reusable enterprise-homepage 3D product-story capability; ROKE is an interaction and narrative reference only, not a product, brand, copy, or asset reproduction target.
Use one generic engine for cars, industrial fittings, consumer electronics, machinery, and other products; keep model-specific groups and choreography in a product-story manifest.
Accept GLB or GLTF input, inspect model structure first, then select true assembly, hybrid reveal, or an explicit degraded capability.
Prefer product-semantic groups, assembly order, and authored directions; do not present a center-radial random explosion as a semantically correct assembly.
For a fused single mesh, support whole-product rotation, reveal, cutaway, or fallback, but do not claim true semantic part assembly without segmentation.

Support a reusable story progression from product introduction through meaningful exploded structure and semantic assembly to complete-product reveal and final hero state with synchronized content and CTA.
Optimize for high-performance modern desktop web rendering; a 4 Mbps weak-network cold-start scenario is not a release criterion.

Compare the GLB runtime and 240-frame image baseline on the same device, browser, and cache conditions using transfer bytes, request count, interactivity, frame time, long frames, main-thread pressure, and memory.
Render on load, scroll, interpolation, resize, or explicit animation demand; do not keep an idle permanent requestAnimationFrame loop.
Preserve an explicit human-review and choreography interface because product grouping, assembly order, camera, lighting, and information emphasis cannot always be inferred from geometry.
